title: Consumers are converting price shocks and institutional failures into attribution, safety routines and value literacy
geography: United States; recurring online consumer-attitudes tracker

tariff_price_expectation.unit: percent saying tariffs will raise prices on goods they buy

tariff_price_attribution.unit: percent saying they have already seen prices rise specifically because of tariffs

tariff_mechanism_knowledge.unit: percent correctly identifying tariffs as import taxes paid by importers that often raise consumer prices

tariff_national_goal_tolerance.unit: percent saying tariff-related price increases are worth it to get what the country wants

tariff_cost_pass_through_fairness.unit: percent saying it is fair for companies to pass tariff costs to shoppers

observations.method: Ipsos Consumer Tracker Wave 148; online panel, partner-panel and river sampling, calibrated to U.S. population targets; credibility interval +/-3.6 percentage points, design-effect-adjusted +/-5.1 points.
observations.uncertainty: These are reported perceptions and policy judgments, not observed tariff incidence, company margins or causal estimates of price changes.
observations.counterinterpretation: Respondents may attribute general inflation or salient price changes to tariffs; the result still matters as a legitimacy and accountability signal because the cost mechanism is becoming publicly legible.

trust_food_safety_inspections.unit: percent expressing a great deal or some trust in government food-safety inspections

recall_trust_decline.unit: percent saying recent food recalls made them trust inspections less

wash_produce.unit: percent saying recalls led them to wash produce at home

avoid_recalled_foods.unit: percent saying recalls led them to avoid recalled foods

buy_local_food.unit: percent saying recalls led them to try to buy more locally sourced foods

buy_less_fresh_produce.unit: percent saying recalls led them to buy less fresh produce at grocery stores

observations.method: Ipsos Consumer Tracker Wave 148 online survey.
observations.uncertainty: The behavior question is select-all-that-apply and measures self-reported response to recalls; it does not verify purchasing or health outcomes.
observations.counterinterpretation: Low trust may coexist with reliance on the inspection system; the key signal is that institutional uncertainty is being converted into household monitoring, localism and avoidance routines.

expensive_not_better.unit: percent saying expensive clothing is not necessarily better quality

brand_less_important.unit: percent saying brand names are becoming less important when shopping for clothing

value_dupe_pride.unit: percent proud to find great value whether a name brand or dupe

fabric_over_brand.unit: percent caring more about fabric than brand name

pay_more_for_durability.unit: percent willing to pay more upfront if clothing will last longer

observations.method: Ipsos Consumer Tracker Wave 148 online survey.
observations.uncertainty: Attitudes toward value and durability are not purchase receipts; category, income and actual garment quality are not separately identified here.
observations.counterinterpretation: Anti-brand sentiment may coexist with selective premium buying; the stronger finding is a shift of evaluative authority toward materials, longevity and perceived value.

police_presence_more_safe.unit: percent saying more police officers on streets make communities safer

armed_federal_presence_more_safe.unit: percent saying armed military or federal agents make communities safer

armed_teachers_more_safe.unit: percent saying teachers openly carrying firearms make communities safer

open_carry_more_safe.unit: percent saying more individuals openly carrying firearms make communities safer

observations.method: Ipsos Consumer Tracker Wave 148 online survey; question measures perceived safety, not crime outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: These are normative perceptions and may vary by political identity, local context and personal exposure; they should not be read as estimates of actual safety effects.
observations.counterinterpretation: The pattern may reflect role legitimacy rather than a general preference for force: respondents distinguish ordinary police presence from militarized, school-based or generalized armed visibility.

related_sources.claim: Official Ipsos Consumer Tracker page announcing Wave 148 tariff findings and linking the topline.

boundary: This record adds a cross-domain mechanism linking tariff attribution, food-safety trust, clothing value literacy and differentiated safety legitimacy. It is an online public-opinion wave, not transaction data, verified household behavior, a crime dataset or a causal policy evaluation.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official Ipsos Wave 148 topline PDF and Consumer Tracker page were retrieved and reviewed for tariff, food-safety, clothing-value and community-safety questions.
